picks.title: Authors Guild Issues AI Guidelines for Publishers
picks.excerpt: The Authors Guild released AI best-practice guidelines for publishers, with a top concern being the growing use of 'imperfect AI detectors' against authors; it follows the Guild's May guidance for authors and aims to ensure mutual trust.
picks.rationale: A new primary policy document: the Authors Guild's first AI best-practice guidelines aimed at publishers, which take direct aim at unreliable AI detectors used against authors.

picks.title: Google launched Expert Intelligence on Google Play Books
picks.excerpt: Eligible Play Books e-books can now be added to Gemini Notebook as grounded sources to generate quizzes, infographics and Audio Overviews; 100,000+ titles from PRH, Macmillan, Bloomsbury and others.
picks.rationale: A concrete product release: purchased Play Books e-books (100,000+ licensed titles from PRH, Macmillan, Bloomsbury) become grounded sources in Gemini Notebook, so readers get a new licensed AI reading feature.

picks.title: AI로 만든 '딸깍 서적' 판치는 한국…저작권 보호는 '걸음마'
picks.excerpt: AI 번역을 그대로 책으로 내는 저품질 '딸깍 출판'이 국내에서 먼저 문제로 부각되는 가운데, AI 기본법에 인간 창작물 보호·AI 창작물 표시 규정이 모호해 저작권 보호가 뒤처졌다는 지적.
picks.rationale: Reports that low-quality 'ttalkkak' books, AI translations printed as-is, are spreading in Korea. It also finds that the AI Basic Act's rules on protecting human work and labelling AI output are too vague to help. That puts AI squarely at the centre of a Korean publishing-quality and copyright gap.

picks.title: 출판인회의 "AI 기업, 학습에 이용한 책에 정당한 보상하라"
picks.excerpt: 한국출판인회의가 '책이 없으면 AI도 없습니다' 호소문 연명을 시작했다. AI 학습은 권리자 이용 허락이 원칙이며, 학습 이용 작품·출처 기록 공개와 정당한 대가 지급을 요구했다.
picks.rationale: The Korean Publishers Society has launched a formal signature campaign, 'No books, no AI'. It demands consent, disclosure of the works used for training, and payment. It is a new collective action following this week's revelations about Anthropic and the bulk book purchases.

alternates.title: Why Are Publishers Suing Big Tech With One Hand and Embracing AI With the Other?
alternates.excerpt: Essay from an Authors Guild 'Whose Truth?' panel on authorship and AI, interrogating publishers who litigate against AI firms while adopting AI tools in-house.
alternates.rationale: Commentary column framed around the Wired 10-10 'publishers quietly using more AI' story, so it is the same running story.
